# Lab 21.1: Editions & Pricing Models

## What We Are Going to Do
Compare on-demand pricing with the Standard, Enterprise and Enterprise Plus editions, and use your own job history to decide which fits a workload.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Read the editions table.** Open the BigQuery **Pricing** page (or **Workload management → Editions**). Note for each edition: price per slot-hour, commitment discounts, and key features (for example, Enterprise for continuous queries and BigQuery ML at scale; Enterprise Plus for managed disaster recovery).

2. **[SQL] Measure your workload.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(total_bytes_billed) / POW(1024, 4), 3) AS tib_billed_30d,
  ROUND(SUM(total_slot_ms) / 1000 / 3600, 2) AS slot_hours_30d,
  ROUND(MAX(total_slot_ms / NULLIF(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(end_time, start_time, MILLISECOND), 0)), 0) AS peak_avg_slots_single_job
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT
WHERE creation_time &gt; TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  AND job_type = 'QUERY' AND statement_type != 'SCRIPT';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Compare the bills.** Replace the prices with the current ones for your region:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">DECLARE on_demand_per_tib FLOAT64 DEFAULT 6.25;
DECLARE standard_per_slot_hr FLOAT64 DEFAULT 0.04;
DECLARE enterprise_per_slot_hr FLOAT64 DEFAULT 0.06;

SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(total_bytes_billed) / POW(1024, 4) * on_demand_per_tib, 2) AS on_demand_usd,
  ROUND(SUM(total_slot_ms) / 1000 / 3600 * standard_per_slot_hr, 2) AS standard_usd_ideal,
  ROUND(SUM(total_slot_ms) / 1000 / 3600 * enterprise_per_slot_hr, 2) AS enterprise_usd_ideal
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT
WHERE creation_time &gt; TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  AND job_type = 'QUERY' AND statement_type != 'SCRIPT';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   "Ideal" assumes autoscaling bills exactly the slots used. Real bills are a little higher.

4. **Decide.** Spiky, small workloads usually stay on-demand. Steady, heavy workloads, or ones that need Enterprise features, move to editions.

5. **[CLI] Check for existing reservations.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq ls --reservation --location=US
bq ls --capacity_commitment --location=US</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| On-demand | Pay per TiB scanned |
| Editions | Pay per slot-hour, with features by tier |
| Your data | Decides, not guesses |
| Commitments | Cheaper slot-hours for 1 or 3 years |
